subject.title: [Bug] Agent context window fragmentation during concurrent subagent tool calls

question: Should concurrent child results remain completion-ordered and identity-labelled, or should a yielded parent always receive them in original spawn order after every required child settles?
rationale: Both contracts are technically viable, but spawn-order buffering changes latency, timeout, and partial-failure behavior; the existing documentation and shipped implementation currently favor event-driven completion and final-child aggregation.

options.title: Keep completion order
options.body: Retain push-based completion semantics, require stable child identity in every result, and fix only a demonstrated misassociation or aggregation defect.

options.title: Adopt spawn-order batches
options.body: Buffer all required child results and flush them in invocation order, accepting head-of-line blocking and defining timeout/failure placeholders.

recommendation.title: Keep completion order
recommendation.body: Retain push-based completion semantics, require stable child identity in every result, and fix only a demonstrated misassociation or aggregation defect.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor guide routes agents/subagents ownership here, and this question defines the public coordination contract for that surface.
